plainLanguageExplanation: A bar chart shows data as bars standing on a category axis (the bottom) and reaching up to a value on the value axis (the side). One bar per category, and the bar's height shows how many — votes, students, dollars, anything counted. To read a bar, run a line from its top to the value axis. The tallest bar shows the biggest category; the shortest shows the smallest. Bar charts make comparing categories a glance instead of a brain-twist.

whyItMatters: Bar charts are the most common chart in the world — election results, budget breakdowns, and survey answers are almost always shown as bars. Reading one is a core life skill.
tagline: Heights that compare at a glance
didYouKnow: Bar charts are one of the oldest chart types — Niclaus of Cusa drew a bar-like chart back in 1440; a full modern bar chart appeared in William Playfair's 1786 atlas, more than two centuries ago.
compareReason: Students reach for the same chart for every purpose — comparing category bars with trend lines shows when each chart is the right tool.
